- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or bullish sentiment; model tends to overshoot in upward momentum phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral, especially after recent declines; model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust for recent sentiment shifts to reduce lag.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model overweights short-term momentum and fails to capture mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative and price is trending up, model often underestimates the upside, missing the “reversal” signal.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong trend, don’t assume continuation unless sentiment confirms it.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to average out, leading to underperformance in sharp directional moves.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is positive but price is flat, model may overreact; if sentiment is negative but price is rising, model may underreact.
